title: I-1 SDK message protocol, v0 (LD-PEC-002 §5). Owner: W2.

CmdInstall.description: Install one product from an inventory lot as a machine or buffer.

CmdRemove.description: Decommission a machine, buffer or connection back into inventory.

from_port.description: Source port: <machine_id>.<port> for a machine port, <buffer_id>.io for a buffer.

to_port.description: Destination port, in the same form as from_port.

CmdConnect.description: Create a connection between two ports.

CmdDisconnect.description: Remove a connection with no material in transit.

CmdCreateJob.description: Create a job for a process on a machine.

CmdStart.description: Make a queued job eligible to run.

CmdPause.description: Pause a job, subject to process constraints.

CmdCancel.description: Cancel a job; work in progress follows its failure disposition.

CmdTransferLocal.description: Move material between buffers over a connection.

CmdSetOperatingPolicy.description: Set a machine's rate setpoint within blueprint limits.

CmdScheduleMaintenance.description: Run a maintenance process on a machine.

CmdCheckpoint.description: Record a history commitment without physical change.

predicate.description: The REQUIRE predicate that failed, exactly as the process declares it (Q-09).

Reason.description: Deterministic explanation of a job's status, tagged by "code": why a started job is not running, or how a running one is limited (DWELLING, FED, FEED_UNSETTLED).

rate.description: Current work rate, in work quanta per microsecond.

unpowered.description: Present and true when the machine's idle draw is not being met (LD-PEC-005 §8.3).

core.description: Contents of the machine's core buffer (<machine>-core), when its blueprint declares one (LD-PEC-004 A2-3). The same material appears in that buffer's view; this is a convenience.

priority.description: Scheduling priority; higher runs first when jobs compete for power or lanes.

energy_held.description: Energy drawn (or, if negative, produced) for work whose units have not completed yet, in the bus unit. It settles into heat and chemical energy when the units complete (LD-PEC-006 §3.2.1).

rate.description: Current work rate, in work quanta per microsecond.

template.description: The catalog buffer template the buffer was installed as.

rate.description: Net charging rate in unit per microsecond: positive while charging (after efficiency), negative while discharging.

EnergyView.description: Bus power in the unit given, per microsecond.

unit.description: Energy unit of supply and demand.

supply.description: Power available on the bus, in energy unit per microsecond (J/µs = MW when unit is j).

demand.description: Power allocated to consumers, in energy unit per microsecond.

throughput.description: Maximum transfer rate, in the connection template's quantity unit per microsecond.

ClaimView.description: Read-only view derived solely from state (LD-PEC-002 §5.4).

lots.description: Every lot on the claim: inventory (products, kits, raw material) and buffer contents. Lots inside a buffer also appear in its BufferView totals.

deposits.description: Deposits on the claim, with what remains and what has been extracted. Each has a face port, <deposit_id>.face, that a FEED can draw from (LD-PEC-005 §3.3).

sinks.description: Material and heat sinks: cumulative losses, tailings and waste heat.

Event.description: Append-only event log entry, tagged by "kind".

NextEventTime.description: t_us is absent when no event is scheduled.

Response.description: Any I-1 response, tagged by "method"; failures use method "error".

ReasonFed.description: A running FLOW job held to the rate its fed inputs arrive at: inputs it alone draws from, drawn as they arrive rather than from reserved stock (LD-PEC-004 A3-1). `ports` lists them in process order.

ReasonFeedUnsettled.description: A running FLOW job held below the rate its fed inputs arrive at: it is in a loop whose fixed point did not settle within the pass limit, so it runs at the last pass of an iteration from below, which every job in the loop can sustain (LD-PEC-004 A3-3). `ports` lists its fed inputs in process order.

ReasonStopLevel.description: A FLOW job stopped at a port's stop level (LD-PEC-004 A4-1): an input's stock fell to it, or an output's free space did. It restarts at the port's restart level.

IssuedBy.description: Which application issued a command (LD-PEC-004 A5, LD-PEC-009 §7). Recorded with the command in its history record, so the hash chain commits to it; it plays no part in physics. The claim host fills it: origin from the browser-verified origin of the sending page, or "host" for the host's own interface. app_name is the application's own description of itself.
